subject: Penetration test retention window, methodology, and firm credentials — acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PT report: acceptance window & firm details

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is finalizing vendor onboarding and has a couple of questions before we close the checklist:

1) For SOC2 evidence, could you confirm the most recent penetration test report you can provide and whether you consider a test from Sep 2026 still valid for acceptance? Our policy requires testing within the last 12 months but we sometimes ask for additional attestation depending on findings.

2) Can you provide a short summary of the testing methodology and the firm credentials (name, accreditation, lead tester) we can include in our procurement notes?

3) Finally, what remediation verification do you offer for high/critical findings — do you provide a re-test or an evidence pack showing fixes?

If you can drop the report and a short methodology blurb to this thread or a secure link, that will speed sign-off.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Security Program Manager
Acme Corp

--
Attachment: none
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PT report: acceptance window & firm details

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we have a September 2026 pen test (attached), we’ll include a methodology summary and firm details below, and we do provide remediation verification — summary and workpapers included with a re-test option if requested. More detail follows from our security lead.

Methodology (brief): Red River Security performed a hybrid blackbox/targeted internal test focused on auth, data plane, and privileged access. Testing followed OWASP ASVS + PTES-aligned approaches and included manual verification of high-risk findings.

Firm (from vendor): Red River Security — CREST-aligned procedures, US-based lead tester (Alex Muir, CREST CRT), 7 years working with cloud SaaS startups.

We’re attaching the vendor report and a short appendix showing the scope for Acme. If you need a signed attestation or a re-test, let us know which findings you want validated and we’ll schedule follow-up with Red River (re-test fees typically apply for scope changes).

Cc’ing Mina and Karthik for remediation verification and formal evidence handoff.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Red River Security <security@redriversec.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: PT deliverables for Redwood / Acme (RR-Security-PT-Report-2026-09)

Evelyn / Jordan —

Attaching the final report and an executive methodology summary. Quick clarifications that Jordan asked about:

- Report date and validity: Report delivered 2026-09-14. Red River considers a 12-month window acceptable for our clients for general acceptance; however, customers with strict policies can request additional attestation (we provide a signed letter describing no material changes in scope since test date).

- Methodology highlights: reconnaissance, automated scanning (SAST/DAST where applicable), manual exploitation, privilege escalation checks, and targeted service account credential reviews. We follow PTES + OWASP mobile/web guidance and use bespoke checks for caching and KV layers specific to Redwood’s runtime.

- Firm credentials: Red River Security — Lead Tester Alex Muir (CREST CRT), Technical Director Priya Anand (CISSP). We operate under an internal QA process with a peer review and have delivered 120+ SaaS engagements since 2019.

- Remediation verification: For high/critical issues we provide a remediation validation package (workpapers, PoC screenshots removed for shared copies) and offer a scoped re-test within 30–90 days at a discounted rate if Redwood opts in. For most SOC2 attestation purposes our attestation letter + remediations workpapers are sufficient.

If you want an additional signed cover letter for Acme’s procurement team we can provide one.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Engagement Manager
Red River Security
security@redriversec.com

--

Subject: Re: PT report: acceptance window & firm details

Eve / Mina —

Thanks for looping Red River in and for the attachments. A couple operational clarifications from our side to make Acme’s procurement form easier:

- Acceptance window: we should confirm whether Acme will accept a 12-month-old report with our signed attestation. I recommend offering the attestation letter that Red River mentioned and a short remediation summary showing fixes applied and verification steps completed.

- Evidence envelope: Mina — can you prepare a redacted workpaper bundle (no PoC code/screenshots) and a one-page remediation log tied to CVE/issue IDs for the top 5 items? That’s usually sufficient for SOC2 reviewers.

- Re-test option: offer a 30–60 day re-test at the discounted rate for any outstanding criticals, and include estimated timeline (we can say 3–4 weeks from sign-off). Jordan, does Acme need the re-test to be completed pre-sign-off or is the attestation + workpapers acceptable?

I’ll draft the attestation letter template and circle back once Mina shares the bundle.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
